body:
Good morning, Bakersfield, and happy Friday. The story leading the day is fire weather: with winds up and the ground dry, utilities have already cut power to thousands of Kern customers and are warning that more shutoffs could run through Saturday. Expect another hot one — a high near 91 — with moderate air quality, no weather alerts, and one active fire burning in the county.

## The Kern Overnight

Deputies and firefighters had a long night, and the strangest call came out of Lamont. Two vehicles collided on East Bear Mountain Boulevard at General Beale Road, out in the rural stretch east of town, and the first units on scene found a large amount of blood on both cars and inside one of them — but nobody who needed an ambulance. The people involved said no one else had been riding with them, and deputies didn't trust that account. They searched the wreckage and the ground around it for anyone who might have been thrown clear, and a sheriff's helicopter was called in to help sweep the area. The investigation stayed open.

Fire carried the middle of the night. A single-wide mobile home in the 200 block of Oswell Street was burning with moderate smoke showing when Battalion 4 arrived. Engine 41 was assigned to pull a line as fire attack, the rest of the assignment split between water supply and search, and crews reported a knockdown a few minutes later, cancelling a second battalion and a truck. Traffic was shut down in both directions on Oswell while hose lines lay across the road. A second house fire drew a full assignment to the 1400 block of Ridgeview Street in east Bakersfield, and a report of a building on fire at 34th Street and San Dimas Street came in just before dawn.

Elsewhere around the county: a woman swung an ax at a man in the 1400 block of Calcutta Drive in south Bakersfield and then left on foot still carrying it; a driver was found unresponsive behind the wheel at White Lane and Buena Vista Road with CPR under way; a man walked into his home in the 3400 block of Granada Avenue with blood on his hands; and a person was reported down on the railroad tracks on Truxtun Avenue approaching Baker Street, where police and medics worked both sides of the crossing while a train crew was asked how long the person had been there.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 91 today and a low around 63 tonight. It's 63 right now at Meadows Field, so the morning is genuinely pleasant before the afternoon turns hot. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is 73, which lands in the moderate range — fine for most of us, but if you're sensitive to smoke or dust, it's worth keeping an eye on through the day. Fire crews are on one active fire in Kern, the Cyrus Fire. With dry, breezy conditions in the forecast, that's the number to watch.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that utilities have already switched off power for thousands of Kern County customers as high winds and dry conditions raise the wildfire risk, and more shutoffs could be coming.** As of 10 p.m. Thursday, Southern California Edison had cut service to 4,251 customers in Kern and PG&E to 593, with notifications sent to thousands more who could be affected. PG&E says roughly 1,100 of its Kern customers could lose power, including 48 on medical baseline, while SCE is weighing outages for more than 20,000 customers here. The potential shutoffs could last into Saturday, so it's worth checking your utility's website and having a plan for refrigerated food, medical equipment and charging.

**KGET 17 reports that one person is dead after an officer-involved shooting in south Bakersfield, and that neighbors have been sharing what they saw.** That is the extent of what we can tell you this morning — the circumstances, the agency involved and the person's identity aren't detailed in what we have in front of us, so we'll pass along more as it's confirmed.

**According to 23ABC, a Bakersfield Christian High School student has founded a nonprofit that opens educational and extracurricular doors for foster youth and underserved children.** Mariana Vargas started For A Better Future USA after befriending a girl named Cristina, who grew up in an orphanage in Mexico and spoke only Spanish when she arrived in the classroom; helping her navigate school showed Vargas how much support some kids go without. The nonprofit partners with local businesses — Kumon, Code Ninjas and Mathnasium among them — to provide scholarships, and Kumon Brimhall owner Vikash Lakhani said two students recruited through the program are expected to begin there soon, with Code Ninjas also offering free coding education.

**KGET 17 reports that the Ward 3 candidates shared a stage for a debate and found plenty of common ground on the issues — they just didn't agree on how to solve them.** The forum gave voters in that part of the city a side-by-side look at the people asking to represent them, which matters most in the final stretch before ballots are cast. We're summarizing from the headline alone here; the station's full report has the specifics of where the candidates split.

## Something good

Vera Varner is 82 years old, and one night a year she gets to be a cheerleader again. Varner told 23ABC that Bakersfield College's homecoming is "almost magical" — a chance to reconnect with fellow alumni and perform at halftime, even if, as she joked, it's like a time machine "until the next day you're so sore you can't move." She's hoping more former BC cheerleaders join her at Saturday's game; she figures there should be at least 600 alumni out there. All you need is red and white and a signed waiver, and the station's story has the details.

Separately, KGET 17 reports the Sherna Armstrong Christmas Benefit Concert is looking for sponsors. If your business wants to help holiday music fill the air this season, that's an open door — and a good one.

## Coming up this week

Tonight, the Fox Theater hosts United We Dance, a festival-energy show built to run all night. Saturday brings the AiAi & Tekla Comedy Tour to the Fox, and it's also Bakersfield College homecoming — the day Vera Varner and her fellow alumni will be back on the field at halftime. Sunday, Fortune Feimster brings her Taking Care of Biscuits tour to the Fox, and Monday the theater's Cults & Classics series screens Psycho. Switchfoot, with special guest Anberlin, plays the Forever Now Tour at the Fox on Wednesday, October 21.

On the public-meeting side, the Historic Preservation Commission meets Tuesday, October 20, at 10 a.m. Bakersfield's City Council has two sessions on Wednesday, October 21 — one at 3:30 p.m. and one at 5:15 p.m. Agendas and locations are posted through the city, so if you've been meaning to weigh in on something, this is the week to show up.

Have a good Friday, and keep an eye on the wind.

top.title: Bakersfield high schooler founds nonprofit bringing educational opportunities to foster, underserved youth
